nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ p ≤ 2` the map `A ↦ A ^ p = cfc (· ^ p) A` is convex on positive-semidefinite complex matrices for the Loewner order: `(t A + (1 - t) B) ^ p ≤ t A ^ p + (1 - t) B ^ p` (E. A. Carlen, *Trace inequalities and quantum entropy: an introductory course*, lecture-notes draft of May 3, 2009, Theorem 2.6). The proof applies Physlib's `LownerHeinzCore.power_Icc_one_two_operatorConvexOn_Ici` to the C⋆-algebra of…
nodes.title: Operator convexity of `t ^ p` for `1 ≤ p ≤ 2` (Loewner–Heinz)

nodes.summary: The map `a ↦ a²` is convex, for the star order, on the convex set of self-adjoint elements of a star-ordered real algebra (E. A. Carlen, *Trace inequalities and quantum entropy: an introductory course*, lecture-notes draft of May 3, 2009, Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.6 with `p = 2`).
nodes.title: The square is operator convex, as a convex function

nodes.summary: There are positive-semidefinite `2 × 2` complex matrices `A ≤ B` (Loewner order) with `A² ≰ B²`: take `A = !![1, 1; 1, 1]` and `B = !![2, 1; 1, 1]`, so that `B - A = !![1, 0; 0, 0] ≥ 0` while `B² - A² = !![3, 1; 1, 0]` has negative determinant. So `t ↦ t²`, monotone on `[0, ∞)`, is not operator monotone; compare the Loewner–Heinz theorem (E. A. Carlen, *Trace inequalities and quantum entropy: an introductory…
nodes.title: The square is not operator monotone

nodes.summary: In any real algebra, `t a² + (1 - t) b² - (t a + (1 - t) b)² = t (1 - t) (a - b)²`. It is the algebraic heart of the operator convexity of `t ↦ t²` (Carlen, *Trace inequalities and quantum entropy*, 2009 draft, Section 2.1).
nodes.title: Convex-combination identity for squares

nodes.summary: For self-adjoint elements `a, b` of a star-ordered real algebra and `0 ≤ t ≤ 1`, `(t a + (1 - t) b)² ≤ t a² + (1 - t) b²`. This is the case `p = 2` of the operator convexity part of the Loewner–Heinz theorem (E. A. Carlen, *Trace inequalities and quantum entropy: an introductory course*, lecture-notes draft of May 3, 2009, Theorem 2.6), stated for every star-ordered real algebra rather than only for matrices.
